reason: The cited evidence (E1, E3) strongly supports the formation of a hard Laves phase and its role in enhancing hardness and wear resistance in a WMoTaNb/316L composite coating on steel. However, the hypothesis applies these findings to a different substrate (TC4) and a pure RHEA coating, without citing evidence for successful laser cladding of WMoTaNb on TC4, the specific optimized parameters, or the minimization of residual stresses on this alloy.
premises: WMoTaNb RHEA can form a hard network Laves phase in a laser-clad coating
This Laves phase significantly increases coating microhardness
Increased microhardness leads to improved wear resistance
Laser cladding can produce a defect-free, well-bonded coating on a steel substrate
Optimized laser parameters can minimize residual stresses and ensure bonding on TC4
